feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads professionally and includes useful scale indicators, but it is somewhat repetitive, overly dense in places, and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap and adding more outcome-based results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure and progression within one organization, plus concrete scope markers like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Broad, relevant capability mix: strategy, governance, CMS, analytics, multimedia, and AI/search are well aligned to target roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add clearer outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities well but not business impact; include more measurable results beyond scale (e.g., engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent (some bullets use serial commas, some do not); “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground scale/relevance: “12+ years leading digital platforms and communications systems for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct outcomes-oriented language: “driving web modernization, governance, analytics, and editorial operations.”
- Reduce the long service list; keep 4–5 priority themes most relevant to target roles: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, AI-enabled search/UX.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; vary the phrasing.
- The list of capabilities repeats core competencies almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, executive-level wording: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “communications operations” with “communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Change “content experiences” to “content discovery” for clearer, more specific meaning.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “systems,” “operations,” and “experiences” unless intentionally grouped.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific phrasing already covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets, so don’t expand it further here.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a short intro line such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: e.g., “Built,” “Developed,” “Led,” and hyphenate consistently (“bill-level,” “AI-enabled”).
- Increase specificity where possible with scale or outcome: audience, platform, campaign purpose, or measurable impact.
- Simplify long noun strings: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” could be shortened for readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo roles; keep this section project-focused and avoid restating responsibilities.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most distinct value because it introduces experiential/display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, strategic advisory value, and only the newest/highest-impact work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal-based campaign delivery, content operations, and AI-enabled search modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 impact-focused bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Replace generic phrasing (“deliver,” “advise,” “develop”) with stronger verbs and outcomes: “Designed,” “Launched,” “Streamlined,” “Led.” Add metrics if possible: number of sites, toolkits, teams supported, time saved, engagement gains, search success improvements.
- Emphasize what is new vs prior employment: consultant remit, AI search initiative, campaign microsites/toolkits, and enterprise advisory work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Drupal platform, microsite structures, modular content sections” duplicates Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement overlap with Director of Digital Media; avoid repeating the same modernization story.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine scope + flagship achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcome language where possible: improved publishing speed, reporting adoption, campaign performance, production cost/time savings, or stakeholder engagement.
- Tighten channel bullet: replace vague audience phrasing with specific list growth, open/click rates, engagement, or campaign results if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/building recurring content may partially overlap with footer projects and earlier video bullets; stress scale-up and in-house capability gains here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and operational improvements specific to this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations line: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and the footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; avoid broad governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctiveness rather than repeating broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing standards & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Digital governance for mission-driven organizations” if you want a more senior, systems-focused tone.
- Keep wording parallel: noun-based phrases, 3–6 words each, no filler.
- If possible, align one phrase to measurable scope from recent work, e.g., “Enterprise web strategy for 10,000+ page platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague and partially duplicated by campaign/storytelling language in recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Put Drupal first and anchor modernization/migration earlier, since recent roles center on Drupal platform rebuilds and AI search.
- Replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and discovery” for cleaner phrasing and stronger alignment with recent project language.
- If possible, tie this section elsewhere to scale: e.g., Drupal modernization supporting a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve specific tools like Airtable/jQuery for Technical + IT if space is tight.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating it verbatim in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics infrastructure, reporting & optimization” or “Analytics, reporting & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items by function: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership reporting • SEO and web performance analysis.”
- Use parallel wording and stronger business language: replace “KPI design” with “KPI framework design” and “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “for enterprise web platforms and decision-making,” without repeating metrics already covered in experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills strategic/capability-focused and leave the full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrase.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production leadership and recent in-house studio/event delivery impact rather than basic task skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to capability + scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to match Director-level experience.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Hybrid event production and live broadcast workflows” for stronger specificity.
- If space allows, align with recent impact: “Built and operated in-house studio capacity for advocacy programming and event coverage.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- PTZ camera systems may be too tool-specific here since Technical + IT already covers detailed tools/workflows.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strategic relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light proficiency context if space allows: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If you want more impact, rename to **CMS & Web Platforms** and align with recent work: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep GitHub Pages only if it supports a real project/example; otherwise replace with a stronger platform or omit.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; consider consolidating or making one broader and this one more specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid overlisting it without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding terms alone.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from raw languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment and automation workflows (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value at this level.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome language elsewhere or here via labels: “used for Drupal microsites, analytics instrumentation, and workflow automation.”
- Consider replacing jQuery with a broader phrase if it’s not a current strength: “JavaScript-based front-end enhancements.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure; keep it here only if you want this section to be the definitive tools list.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and more systems-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to group by function and emphasize implementation strength, e.g.: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.”
- Remove basic collaboration tools unless they are central to systems design; Slack and Teams are too commonplace and dilute the section.
- If accurate, add a qualifier for impact: “used to build editorial planning, intake, approval and cross-team coordination workflows.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” to better match the seniority and content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project tools—listing all four may feel padded unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and under-leverages your recent leadership in email operations. It should signal enterprise-scale platform ownership rather than read like a basic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: **Higher Logic (enterprise member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Mailchimp (newsletter/campaign delivery)**
- If space allows, tie to outcomes-oriented capability instead of pure tools: **Email platform administration, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and campaign automation across Higher Logic, Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys and Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Your work history already covers email leadership; avoid repeating “newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here unless you remove similar phrasing elsewhere.
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader multi-channel communications claims in Core Competencies; keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics points already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize methods and business use, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace with a sharper mix of tools + capabilities: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • dashboard development • SEO analysis • experimentation / A/B testing**
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- If space allows, make terminology more senior/strategic: use **KPI design** and **experimentation** instead of generic **dashboarding** and **A/B testing**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in only one place.
- “Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure…” in the Director role already validates these tools, so avoid repeating the exact same phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate’s daily production work.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume supported, audience growth, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame it as early process-building rather than organization-wide leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the launch/ownership angle and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast line more active and concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or types of research projects supported.
- Consider framing this as a bridge into digital leadership: highlight content production support rather than broad “contributed to digital content production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and research/program coordination.
- Avoid repeating generic “supporting organizational programs and policy work” if stronger specifics are available.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed tools/functions list than a sharp technical skills entry. It also overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere, so it should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
